newsitem.title: USA: Schools focus of Wis. governor state of state talk.
newsitem.headline: Schools focus of Wis. governor state of state talk.

text.p: Wisconsin Gov. Tommy Thompson outlined a plan to reshape schools in his state of the state address to the legislature Wednesday evening.

In a speech peppered with references to the Super Bowl Champion Green Bay Packers, the Republican governor called on lawmakers "to prepare Wisconsin's schools to meet the challenges of a new millennium."
The governor proposed a $500 million, five-year technology program that would be partially funded with bonds to give schools computer hardware, software and training.

He said his upcoming fiscal 1998-99 biennial budget would include $65 million in local grants for school districts and that $50 million in annual bonding would be available to loan to schools for upgrading electrical and network wiring.
"Even though this will be a tight budget, we must make a long-term investment in the future of our children," he said.
The state must provide two-thirds of the cost of local schools in the upcoming budget, under a property tax relief plan in effect.

Thompson vowed to continue his fight for a school choice program in Milwaukee that was ruled unconstitutional earlier this month by the Dane County Circuit Court because it allowed state money to be used to send children to church-based schools.
In the meantime, Thompson said he would push for public school choice by providing more options for technical education. He also called for "rigorous academic standards" at schools.

Thompson also said he would announce next week "the boldest environmental initiative in this state in a generation" aimed at cleaning up contaminated urban sites and improving the state's clean water program.
He added that his upcoming budget, scheduled to be unveiled Feb 12, would include a "comprehensive public safety package."
Senate Majority Leader Chuck Cvala, D-Madison, said the state of the state address sounded like a Democratic speech.
He said Democrats in the legislature would support the school technology initiative and would want to see more details of the governor's environmental plan.
